title: Characteristic Equation Method
summary: Algebraic method to solve linear recurrence equations with constant coefficients using the characteristic polynomial. Includes applicability, ERLH, distinct roots, repeated roots, non-homogeneous cases, Fibonacci, Towers of Hanoi and frequent errors.

learningObjectives.text: Recognize when a recurrence is linear homogeneous with constant coefficients.
Detect when the characteristic equation does not apply directly, especially in divide and conquer recurrences.
Transform a recurrence into its characteristic polynomial using the substitution T(n)=r^n.
Calculate real, complex or repeated roots of the characteristic polynomial.
Build the general solution from the roots and their multiplicities.
Use initial conditions to solve for the constants of the general solution.
Identify the dominant root and translate the closed solution to asymptotic order.
Solve the Fibonacci recurrence using characteristic equation.
Resolve simple non-homogeneous recurrences by separating homogeneous solution and particular solution.

terms.label: ERLH
terms.definition: Homogeneous Linear Recurrence Equation. It is linear because the terms T appear to the power 1, homogeneous because it has no external term independent of T, and it has constant coefficients.

terms.label: characteristic polynomial
terms.definition: Polynomial obtained by substituting T(n)=r^n into a homogeneous linear recurrence and dividing by the lowest common power of r.

terms.label: characteristic root
terms.definition: Value of r that satisfies the characteristic polynomial.

terms.label: Multiplicity
terms.definition: Number of times a root appears repeated in the characteristic polynomial.

terms.label: General solution
terms.definition: Closed form of T(n) expressed as a combination of terms constructed from the characteristic roots.

terms.label: dominant root
terms.definition: Root with highest absolute value. Determines the principal asymptotic growth when there is no cancellation due to initial conditions.

terms.label: Forcing term
terms.definition: External term g(n) in a non-homogeneous recurrence, for example +1, +n or b^n·p(n).

terms.label: particular solution
terms.definition: Additional part of the solution used to capture the effect of the forcing term on a non-homogeneous recurrence.
